QUICK ANSWERS / FAQ

Common questions.
Direct answers.

What is the OpenMausBot Python MCP bridge?

An independent Python stdio proxy built with FastMCP. It connects MCP clients to the vendor mcp-server.js shipped with an installed OpenMausBot app, preserving tool schemas and results while enforcing an explicit tool allowlist.

How do I connect OpenMausBot to ChatGPT?

Install the bridge, configure OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel to launch it, add a custom MCP plugin using the authorized tunnel, and enable that plugin in a chat. Verify with actual health and bot-list tool calls. See the step-by-step ChatGPT setup.

Does the Python bridge need an OpenAI API key?

No. The separate OpenAI tunnel client needs a restricted runtime credential. The vendor app may require its own paired session token for actions.

Can I use it without ChatGPT?

Yes. A compatible local MCP client can launch the bridge directly over stdio, without the OpenAI tunnel.

Can ChatGPT send instructions to bots?

The bridge supports message-sending tools, but actions are disabled by default. Enable them explicitly with --allow-writes, satisfy app pairing requirements, restart the connection and refresh discovery.

Is this an official plugin?

No. It is an independent MIT-licensed integration. OpenMausBot, OpenAI and all third-party dependencies retain their own ownership and licenses.

Which versions are verified?

Local tests used Windows, Python 3.14.7, FastMCP 2.14.7, MCP SDK 1.30.0 and packaged OpenMausBot server 0.1.118. Other versions have not been certified. Run unit and live verification after updates.

Does publishing this site expose my bots?

No. This site contains public documentation only. Your app, private tunnel profiles, credentials and transcripts are not part of the website.
